scenes.title: Six Forty-Five
scenes.summary: At dawn M1 draws F1 a street map to the old hardware shop across the bridge before guests wake up.
scenes.intro: It is six forty-five in the morning at the {SHOW} in {CITY}. While the guests still sleep upstairs, {M1} sketches a quick street map on paper for {F1}. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: Good morning, {M1}! Are the showers upstairs really cold already?
Cold as river water. Take this broken brass valve in your coat pocket.
Got it. Now tell me how to find the hardware shop.
Turn left outside our gate and walk straight to the stone bridge.
Left at the gate, straight to the bridge. Do I cross the river?
Yes, cross the bridge, then pass the green pharmacy on your right.
Bridge, then green pharmacy on the right. And after that?
Turn left into the small square. Look for a blue wooden door.
Does the shop have a big sign outside?
Only a painted golden key above the door. Show the clerk this valve.
Twenty millimetres, brass, boiler valve—I will repeat it all the way!
Run fast, {F1}. Room four wakes up at seven fifteen!
scenes.outro: Left at the gate, across the bridge, past the green pharmacy, and left into the square—{F1} is off on her dawn mission. See you next time.

scenes.title: The Blue Door
scenes.summary: Across the river F1 calls M1 from the square to check the last turn and finds the right brass valve.
scenes.intro: Ten minutes later, {F1} has crossed the river bridge in {CITY}, yet two narrow streets branch off behind the pharmacy. She phones {M1} from beside a stone fountain. Listen first.
story: {M1}, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!
Loud and clear. Are you standing by the little stone fountain?
Yes! There are two small streets on the left—which one do I take?
Take the second street, beside the flower stall, not the narrow alley.
Walking now... oh, I see the golden key sign and the blue door!
The clerk is unlocking it right now! Stay on the phone one second.
Make sure the brass ring inside is twenty millimetres wide.
He matched it against the old one—he has two left on the shelf!
Buy both! A spare valve saves next winter too.
Paid in cash! Keep your toolbox open, I am running back across the bridge!
Hurry—I just heard footsteps on the second-floor stairs!
scenes.outro: Two new brass valves in her pocket and early risers already stirring upstairs! Next time, {F2} and {M2} try to keep everyone busy at breakfast.

scenes.title: Hot Cinnamon Rolls
scenes.summary: Downstairs F2 and M2 tempt early-rising F3 with fresh cinnamon rolls before anyone turns on a cold tap.
scenes.intro: Back at the guesthouse, {F3} walks down at seven ten in her dressing gown, hoping for tea before her morning wash. {F2} and {M2} exchange a quick look and launch their distraction plan. Listen first.
story: Good morning! Something smells like warm cinnamon all the way upstairs!
Good morning, Madam {F3}! My cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
Sit right down by the sunny window, madam! No rush to go upstairs yet!
Actually, I only came down to ask why the bathroom tap felt so chilly.
Chilly? Ah—yes! Our neighbourhood water pipes take a gentle morning stretch!
Have a hot cup of tea and a cinnamon roll for ten minutes first!
Well, nobody wise says no to warm cinnamon bread at seven in the morning.
Wonderful choice! Would you like honey or apple jam beside it?
Just a little butter, thank you. Why are you looking at your watch, sir?
Me? Oh, I simply love punctuality! Seven fourteen is a beautiful minute!
Look through the courtyard window, {M2}—someone just ran through the gate!
Saved! Excuse me one moment, madam, enjoy your hot tea!
scenes.outro: Warm cinnamon rolls bought the exact ten minutes they needed as {F1} dashed back through the courtyard gate. Let's head down to the boiler room next time.

scenes.title: Down in the Cellar
scenes.summary: In the cellar M1 and F1 swap in the new brass valve and bring hot water roaring back through the house.
scenes.intro: Down in the brick cellar beneath the courtyard, {F1} hands {M1} the new brass valve while holding a bright flashlight on the silent boiler. Listen first.
story: Here are both brass valves, {M1}! Catch my breath? Never!
Hold this flashlight steady on the pipe joint right here.
Got it! Did you turn off the main water tap already?
Off and drained. Pass me the heavy wrench on your left.
This big iron one? Here you go.
One turn, two turns... look how clean that new brass thread fits.
No drips at all! Can we light the boiler now?
Open the blue wheel slowly to the left—not too fast.
Turning slowly... listen! Water is rushing in!
And there goes the burner flame—steady blue, just how it should be.
Touch the copper pipe! It is warming up already!
Three minutes to reach the third floor. Good run today, partner.
scenes.outro: A steady blue flame and hot copper pipes—and {M1} even called {F1} 'partner' instead of 'rookie'! Let's go upstairs next time as {M3} comes down from the attic.

scenes.title: Five-Star Showers
scenes.summary: M3 praises the hot shower at breakfast while flustered M2 accidentally hints that they read his notebook.
scenes.intro: Twenty minutes later in the sunny café corner, {M3} comes down looking refreshed as {F1} pours coffee and anxious owner {M2} hovers nearby. Listen first.
story: Good morning, {F1}! Good morning, sir! What a bright morning after the rain.
Good morning, {M3}! Did you sleep well under the roof beams?
Best sleep I have had all month, and the shower water was wonderfully hot!
Hot! Hear that, {F1}? Reliable, modern, five-star hot water!
Old brick buildings usually take ages to warm up on the top floor.
Please write that down! 'Hot water on the third floor: ten out of ten!'
Excuse me? Ten out of ten?
What {M2} means is... we hope every guest feels ten out of ten here!
No, {F1}, let us be honest professionals! Sir, we respect the {CITY} Travel Guide!
The {CITY} Travel Guide? Wait—do you think I am a hotel inspector?
When your notebook fell open on the counter last night, we saw 'nine out of ten'...
Oh! Come outside to the courtyard for a minute—let me show you what I really do!
scenes.outro: {M2} spilled the secret in record time, and instead of looking stern, {M3} burst out laughing! Let's step into the courtyard next time to learn his real job.

scenes.title: The Acoustic Architect
scenes.summary: Under the courtyard tree, M3 shows F1 and F2 his sketches: he studies quiet courtyard acoustics, not hotel stars.
scenes.intro: Out under the old shade tree in the courtyard, {M3} opens his brown leather notebook for {F1} and {F2} while morning birds sing overhead. Listen first.
story: Look closely at this page—it measures decibels and quietness, not hotel stars!
Decibels? So 'nine out of ten' was not a review of my check-in?
Well, your check-in deserves ten! Honestly, though, I am an acoustic architect.
An acoustic architect! You design concert halls?
Small libraries and courtyards, mostly. I measure how old stone walls block street noise.
That is why you listened for cars up in the attic last night!
Exactly. Outside on the avenue it is loud, yet inside this courtyard you hear leaves and birds.
Wait until {M2} hears he panicked all night over decibels!
Truthfully, I also chose this neighbourhood for an old family reason.
Oh? Did your family live near here once?
Two streets away, when I was small. Friday is... an important day for me.
scenes.outro: {M3} is an acoustic architect—and that quiet mention of 'two streets away' and 'Friday' just made {F1} and {F2} trade a wide-eyed look! See you next time.

scenes.title: Sunlight on the Tag
scenes.summary: While airing out the luggage closet, M1 brings out the blue suitcase and F3 recognises the old address in daylight.
scenes.intro: At midday, {M1} opens the hallway closet to air it out after the storm and sets the unclaimed blue suitcase beside the front desk, just as {F3} walks in to speak with {F1}. Listen first.
story: Let me set this blue suitcase here for five minutes while I sweep the closet.
Careful with it, {M1}—Friday at noon is tomorrow!
Oh, is that the twin suitcase from Monday's train?
Yes, madam, still waiting for its owner.
May I look at the paper tag again here in the bright sunlight?
Go right ahead, madam. Monday afternoon the lobby was dark.
Wait a moment... Number twelve, {STREET}, and two childhood initials written in the corner!
Madam {F3}, you look amazed! Do you know Number twelve, {STREET}?
Know it? Every Friday for six years I climbed those wooden stairs to teach piano!
Twenty-five years ago? In that same house?
A carpenter lived there with his two grandsons—the older boy played piano, and the little one loved trains!
A carpenter... and a little wooden toy train inside the bag!
scenes.outro: Bright daylight on an old luggage tag just unlocked twenty-five years of history: two brothers on {STREET} and their grandfather's wooden train! One scene left in Episode 4—see you next time.

scenes.title: The Boy on the Stairs
scenes.summary: In the courtyard F3 describes the quiet younger brother listening from the stairs just as M3 walks out and hears her.
scenes.intro: Stepping out into the sunlit courtyard, {F3} tells {F1} more about the two brothers from Number twelve, unaware that {M3} has just walked down the outdoor stairs behind them. Listen first.
story: Tell me more about the two boys on {STREET}, Madam {F3}!
The older brother was bold and loud, always rushing through his music scales.
And the younger brother with the wooden train?
Quiet as a mouse! He sat on the third stair listening to every single note.
Listening to the sound of the room... wait a second!
Whenever I finished playing, he asked why the piano sounded warmer when it rained.
Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo from the cobblestones...
Good heavens... look at your eyes! Little {M3} from the third stair?!
Madam {F3}?! My brother's Friday piano teacher?!
Wait—then Monday night on our doorstep... the second blue suitcase...
Yes, {F1}. That blue suitcase is mine—and I owe you both the whole truth.
scenes.outro: What a moment in the courtyard: little {M3} from the third stair is standing right in front of his childhood piano teacher—and he is the mystery suitcase owner! Episode 4 is complete; see you in Episode 5.
